text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The high price rise for petroleum products causes a surprise. The new government raised prices by 15-32 percent.
- Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit says jailed editor Isik Yurtcu, to be visited by a group of Western journalists on Wednesday, will be released by the end of July.
MILLIYET
- Turkey will be left out of the European Union in the year 2000 according to a copy of an EU report which does not mention Turkey on its full-membership list.
- Three deputies resign from the conservative True Path Party, the junior coalition partner in the previous Islamist-led government.
HURRIYET
- The secularist government appoints new bureaucrats to positions which the Islamists had previously filled with their supporters.
- A missile is fired at a military hostel in central Istanbul, causing one minor injury. Leftist guerrillas are believed to be responsible.
YENI YUZYIL
- State organisations are among the leading tax debtors.
- Two workers die and four are injured in a natural gas leak in central Istanbul.
RADIKAL
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz and leftist leader Deniz Baykal agree to investigate further a security scandal over ties between the state and underworld gangs.
CUMHURIYET
- Yilmaz's government seeks to provide financial support for the public Ziraat Bankasi, cash-strapped because of the policies of the previous coalition.
DUNYA
- Workers at the privatised tyre-maker Petlas are to go on strike on Tuesday in the absence of any agreement on collective contracts.
ZAMAN
- The General Staff plans to disband a special working group formed to monitor Islamist activism.
